components.name: Step and speed faders
components.description: Short detented faders in the joint and tool banks: legend and value above a slot as wide as the channel, the range's ends printed under it. The detents are the values the server accepts (joint step 0.1-15 deg, speed 1-120 deg/s, each joint capped at 80% of its servo's own limit; tool step 0.1-50 mm, turn 0.1-15 deg, speed 1-1000 mm/s with a detent at 250), so the cap only rests where the arm will take it. Same cap, groove and fader-cap shadow as the joint meters; arrow keys step a detent; screen readers hear the value with its unit in words. Channels on a row stand 24px apart with a 1px seam between them. The speed faders mark their slow default (10 deg/s, 20 mm/s) with a longer tick and go back to it every time the panel opens; steps are remembered. Above a joint's top speed, the joint speed fader prints the joints it limits between its range ends ("J1-2 max 84, J3 114.5, J4-6 119.1"). Like a speedometer's red zone, each speed fader prints a redline where the flange could pass 250 mm/s (ISO 10218's limit for jogging by hand): a 2px Alarm Red rule along the ticks' feet, clear of the focus ring, from the line to the top of the scale; the ticks past it, the top figure and the line's own figure ('250', or '17' on joint speed, hidden where it would touch an end figure or the top-speed note) in Alarm Red; and the value in Alarm Red while the cap sits past it. The message line says why on every move into or within the red, with the flange's speed rounded up to 10 mm/s, and again when the cap leaves it or the line moves past a resting cap (not during drags or moves). Tool speed's redline is fixed at 250 mm/s, a detent of its own. Joint speed's follows the arm's pose (the slowest speed at which one joint alone would swing the flange past 250 mm/s) and any staged plan's path (joints turning in step add up; the plan note turns red with the figure), showing whichever is lower, since the jog keys still turn one joint at this speed; it assumes full reach until the pose is known, and a crossing made while the arm moves is reported once it settles. Keyboard focus rings the slot itself, with no offset. In Windows High Contrast the cap, ticks and seams take system colours and focus shows as a system-colour outline. Faders share a bank row in equal widths (150-320px) and take the full width each under 560px. The monitor's Reset view and the plan bar's Clear stay small 30px keys.

components.name: 3D monitor
components.description: The ARM section: bank with title, legend and Reset view key over the sunk screen, with the floating drag readout (clear and blocked) and the plan bar docked along the screen's bottom while a pose is staged (it covers the grey help line). In the build the arm stands on its cart above the floor; the camera fits a sample of the arm's and cart's mesh points inside 14px margins and an 80px band kept for the plan bar (at most 30% of a short screen), re-frames on resize unless the user has turned or zoomed, and Reset view re-frames. A fader drag anchors the readout just outside that joint's ring, away from the links that follow it (J6: away from J5). A blocked plan shows a flat 14px contact mark (Alarm Red core, hard 2px Well Black rim, constant size on screen) where it first comes within 10mm of something and a faint red overlay with red edges on the cart part it would hit, never a red wash; Move then stays pressable but unlit, and a press gets the refusal ring and the reason on the message line. Under 520px of screen width the plan bar drops its legend and each chip's from-angle ('J2 → −20.0°'; the strips still show it), and its note sits beside the keys; on a phone (560px and below) the screen is half the window's height, 360px to 500px; on a screen at least 640px wide and more than 1.6 times as wide as tall (the stacked side panel) it docks at the bottom-right in a 248px column with the help line, and the camera frames arm and cart in the full height. The WebGL scene itself (URDF arm on its cart, tape-coloured rings, amber shadow arm, path line, floor grid) is not reproduced here. When a staged move at the chosen speed would carry the flange past the 250 mm/s redline, the plan note turns Alarm Red at regular weight and adds how fast. The bank also holds the Joints/Tool mode keys; the legend's drag sample reads 'drag a ring' (a Sky Tape ring) in Joints mode and 'drag an arrow or ring' (a ring in the gizmo's three axis colours) in Tool mode, and the help line speaks for the mode in use. In Tool mode the camera framing keeps the whole gizmo on screen, keeps a band as tall as the plan bar while it shows (up to half the screen), and re-frames when a newly staged pose leaves the gizmo near an edge or under the bar, unless the user has turned or zoomed; it never re-frames during a drag. A gizmo drag's readout sits just outside the gizmo toward the pointer, or, with no room there, centred above or below it, 120px from its centre.

components.name: Tool gizmo
components.description: Shown in Tool mode at the flange of the shadow arm, with its axes along the arm's base frame. Three arrows (a 3px shaft from 16px to 74px, a 20px cone tipped at 94px) and three rings 58px in radius, one about each arrow's axis, with printed letters X, Y, Z (18px bold, 2px Well Black outline) 108px out and the rings' names Rx, Ry, Rz (13px, the same print) 76px out, each at whichever of its ring's four diagonals reads best from the camera (near side, clear of the arrows, letters and other names; it holds its place until another is clearly better). Each axis wears its colour, as in other 3D tools, on its arrow, ring, letter and ring name: X Axis Red (#ff3352), Y Axis Green (#8bdc00), Z Axis Blue (#2890ff), over a 1.7px Well Black rim, drawn over everything at a fixed size on screen; the letters stay, so colour is never the only cue. Each ring's far half, facing away from the camera, is drawn at 35%, so the cage reads in depth (a ring seen face-on is drawn whole). Dims to 30% when locked and for the other handles during a drag; the hovered handle brightens a third of the way to white, keeping its hue, with a translucent band of its colour; a dragged arrow lights amber, like a held key; a dragged ring lights white and its turn is the amber: a 45% wedge edged by a heavier arc (both Alarm Red when blocked); on a ring seen nearly side-on the wedge flattens into the arc, and the readout carries the angle. Arrows slide the flange in 1mm steps (10mm with Shift), rings turn it in place in 0.5-degree steps (5 with Shift); the joints follow by inverse kinematics from the pose before, the drag stops at the last reachable pose, and release stages every joint the solution turns. A WebGL object, so the sample is a flat SVG rendering of it, turning about Ry (the other handles, which dim during a real drag, are shown undimmed).

narrative.overview:
The jog panel is a mixing desk for a robot arm. Each of the six joints is a channel strip: a length of coloured scribble tape with the joint's name, a plus key, a vertical meter with a ladder of lead lights beside it, a minus key and a readout. The meter shows where the joint is (a solid fader cap that can be grabbed and dragged) and where it was sent (a hollow amber frame); the lead lights count the steps the joint still has to go and go out as it catches up. A 3D monitor, stacked above the faders in the owner's app side panel and beside them on wide screens, shows the arm itself, standing on its cart above the floor, with a ring at each joint in that joint's tape colour: dragging rings (or the meters' fader caps) stages a pose, shown by an amber shadow arm, and nothing moves until Move sends it. The tool gets a master section of six axis rows. A meter bridge across the top carries the link lamp, the machine state, the hold-to-enable key and an oversized red STOP; a message line is pinned along the bottom.

The desk is matte charcoal and dense, with every control on screen at once. Colour is light, not paint: the keys are identical charcoal caps, and colour appears only to report state. Amber is reserved for held keys and motion, green for live and powered, red for stopped, faulted or unreachable, and for moves that are refused or blocked. The owner watches the arm more than the screen, so the state reads at a glance: one big state word in a window that lights up, one big red key. Light is flat and never glows. Motion is short and mechanical, mostly on one quick ease-out curve, and switches off when reduced motion is requested.

The panel rejects Umbratek Studio's grey round buttons floating over a 3D viewport. Its 3D view is a monitor sunk into the desk, the controls inside it are the joints' own rings, and the only panels over the picture are a readout while a drag is under way and the plan bar docked along its bottom while a pose is staged. Every other control is a square key with a printed legend, mounted on the desk.
keyCharacteristics: Matte charcoal desk; depth comes from recessed wells, flat panels and raised key caps.
Square backlit keys; colour only reports state: amber held or moving, green live, red stop or fault.

Step and speed set on small detented faders, the same cap and slot as the joint faders, snapping to the values the arm accepts, with a speedometer-style redline wherever the flange could pass 250 mm/s.
One scribble-tape colour per joint, carried onto that joint's ring in the 3D monitor.

A sunk 3D monitor where dragging joints' rings or their fader caps, or a gizmo at the flange whose arrows and rings move the tool while the joints follow, stages a pose shown by an amber shadow arm, which Move sends as one move; the arm stands on its cart, and a pose that would hit anything turns red.
Amber lead lights that count the steps a joint still has to travel.
One system sans family, tabular figures, uppercase printed legends.
A sticky meter bridge with STOP, the biggest key, at its top-right, and a message line pinned to the bottom.
Keys travel: a hard 2px bottom edge that collapses when pressed.

rules.name: The Backlight Rule
rules.body: Keys are charcoal at rest. Colour on the desk is light that reports state: amber for held keys and motion, green for live and motors on, red for stop, fault, no signal and refusal, and for speeds past the redline. Focus is drawn in Legend Ink, and nothing is coloured for decoration: besides the state colours, only the tapes, which name joints, and the gizmo's axis colours, which name axes, carry hue.

rules.name: The Brightness Ladder Rule
rules.body: The state window's tones differ in brightness, not just hue. From brightest to darkest: MOVING lit solid amber, an alarm in solid red, READY lit green, STOPPED or PAUSED in a dark red tint, MOTORS OFF or CONNECTING in a plain dark well. Stale status drops any lit tone except alarm to that dark well and keeps the word.

rules.name: The One Red Key Rule
rules.body: STOP is the only key with a red face, and the alarm state window is the only other solid red. Elsewhere red is a lamp, a word, a rim, a 2px ring, a tick or a printed rule, and it marks a refused or blocked move, or a speed past the redline: the red shadow arm, arc, path and readout border, the red contact mark and the red overlay on the part it would hit, the red goal frame on a fader, and the red zone on a speed fader.

rules.name: The Tape Rule
rules.body: Each joint keeps its tape colour, in joint order, on its scribble strip, its meter's lit column and its ring in the 3D monitor, and nowhere else (the legend's ring sample borrows tape 2). Tape names a joint; its hue never reports state.

rules.name: The Axis Colour Rule
rules.body: The tool gizmo colours X, Y and Z red, green and blue, as 3D tools do, and nothing else wears those three colours (the Tool legend's ring sample borrows them). They name an axis and never report state: a dragged arrow lights amber and a blocked turn goes Alarm Red, as everywhere. The printed letters stay, so colour is never the only cue, as for someone who can't tell red from green.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure is tabular, set once for the whole page, with fixed decimals: two for joint angles, one for tool values and drag targets. Digits never shuffle while the arm moves.

rules.name: The Printed Legend Rule
rules.body: Names of groups, settings and channels are printed: uppercase, semibold or bold, tracked 0.06 to 0.1em. Machine states are uppercase words, even inside a message ("STOP NOT CONFIRMED: press the hardware E-stop now."). Instructions, values, units and messages otherwise stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Bridge Stays Rule
rules.body: The meter bridge and the message line never scroll away, and STOP is always at the bridge's top-right.

rules.name: The First Screenful Rule
rules.body: Stacked, the monitor stays short enough (clamp(300px, 36vh, 500px)) and the fader meters compact enough (clamp(170px, 22vh, 280px)) that the fader readouts still land in the first screenful; side by side, at 1241px and wider, the monitor stays pinned in view while the faders scroll.

rules.name: The Up Is Plus Rule
rules.body: On a strip, + sits above the meter and − below, matching the meter's scale (+180 at the top) and the lead lights (a + lead lights upward). Tool rows read − on the left and + on the right.

rules.name: The Key Travel Rule
rules.body: A pressed key moves: its 2px edge collapses, the cap drops 2px (STOP 3px) and the shadow turns inward, over 120ms (STOP 100ms). Hover only brightens the cap a step; nothing lifts.

rules.name: The Sunk Display Rule
rules.body: The state window, the 3D screen, the meters, the lead ladders and the message line are wells; keys are raised caps; sections and strips stay flat between them.

rules.name: The Flat Light Rule
rules.body: Lit things are flat: lamps, lead lights and lit state windows never glow, the joint rings are flat unlit colour, and the shadow arm is self-lit and translucent without a halo. The only coloured shadows are hard 2px rings: the refusal ring and the activity ring.

rules.name: The Square Key Rule
rules.body: Every key is a squared cap with 4px corners (STOP 6px). No key is round or pill-shaped; round belongs to lamps and joint rings.

rules.name: The Biggest Key Rule
rules.body: No key is bigger or louder than STOP: the only red face, the largest legend on the page, the full height of the bridge, with its shortcuts printed on it.

rules.name: The Hold-to-Commit Rule
rules.body: Switching the motors on is a hold, not a click: the green bar must fill the key's lower edge before anything happens.

rules.name: The Stage-then-Move Rule
rules.body: Dragging a ring, a gizmo handle or a joint's fader cap only stages: the shadow arm, arc, path and readout show the plan, and nothing moves until Move sends every staged joint as one move. Esc backs out a drag, then the plan; a blocked plan can't be sent, and the server checks every plan again.

rules.name: The Dash Rule
rules.body: An unknown value is an em dash (—) with an empty meter and dark lead lights, never a zero and never the last known number.

dos: Do keep every key except STOP a charcoal cap with 4px corners, a 1px rim and a 2px hard bottom edge, lit amber only while it is held.
Do print group and setting names as uppercase legends (11px, 600, 0.08em, Printed Grey), and channel names on their tape (12px, 700, uppercase, Marker Black).
Do give each joint its tape colour, in joint order, on its scribble strip, meter column and 3D ring only.

Do show a commanded value only while the joint or axis is still travelling to it: a hollow amber frame on the meter, amber lead lights counting the steps to go, an amber "→ value" line and, for joints, the amber shadow arm. A staged angle is planned, not commanded: a dashed frame and a grey "→ value" until Move sends it.
Do keep the 3D monitor a sunk screen in the desk, with the joints' own rings, or the gizmo at the flange, as its controls.
Do colour the gizmo's axes red, green and blue (X, Y, Z) over a Well Black rim, and still name its axes and rings with printed letters; light a dragged arrow amber, and draw a ring's turn in amber.
Do set the floating readout just outside the ring, outward from its centre (and, for a fader drag, away from the links that follow), so it never covers the ring or its arc.
Do keep STOP the biggest key, red, at the top-right of the sticky bridge, with its keyboard shortcuts printed on it.
Do set step and speed on detented faders that can only rest on values the arm accepts, with the value above and the range printed under the ends; start the speeds slow every time.

Do print a redline on the speed faders, like a speedometer's red zone with its figures, wherever the flange could pass 250 mm/s, and let the joint speed redline follow the arm's pose and any staged plan, whichever is lower.
Do make each state-window tone differ from the others in brightness as well as hue.
Do draw the focus ring in Legend Ink (2px, 2px offset; tight around a fader's slot).
Do put displays in recessed wells, and keep sections and strips flat with 1px seams.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better against its ground, as every built pair does except Printed Grey on key caps and STOP's dimmed sub-line.
donts: Don't float grey round buttons over a 3D view of the arm, as Umbratek Studio's Live Control does.
Don't make any key round or pill-shaped; only lamps and the 3D monitor's rings are round.
Don't use the axis colours anywhere but the gizmo and its legend sample, or let them report state: a dragged arrow lights amber and a blocked move goes Alarm Red, as everywhere.
Don't give any key but STOP a red face; a refused key gets a red ring and legend on a darkened cap.
Don't wash the 3D scene red for a blocked move; a red contact mark and a red overlay on the part it would hit say where.
Don't use amber for focus or decoration; it means a held key or motion.
Don't use green or red as decoration, or tape colours for state.
Don't make lights glow; lamps, lead lights, rings and lit windows are flat, and the only coloured shadows are hard 2px rings.
Don't show a zero or the last known number when a value is unknown; show an em dash and an empty meter.
Don't add a second type family or proportional figures.
Don't put shadows on sections or strips; shadows belong to keys, fader caps, wells, the sticky bridge, the floating readout and the plan bar.
